description: Movement library metadata for Tibi (Cobalt Sculpt). Kinematics are in src/studio/kits/fitness/exercises.js under the same ids. The 12 upper-body exercises come from the verified research of projects/upper-body-workout (research.md table, dossier claims c14-c26): muscles name the main contributors from standard texts (NSCA Essentials 4e; OpenStax A&P 2e), cues and alternatives are coaching guidance, not research findings. No activation percentages; no exercise isolates one muscle.
kinematics_note: Joint angles are authored from typical ranges, not measured motion capture. Label any on-screen angle 'illustrative' unless a cited study supplies it.

exercises.name: Push-up
exercises.start: Hands just outside shoulder width, body one straight line from head to heels (ribs down, glutes tight).

phases.description: Lower the chest to the floor with elbows angled back, not flared straight out.
Push the floor away and finish with the shoulder blades spread around the ribcage.

muscles.fibres: pectoralis-major; triceps-brachii; deltoid (anterior fibres) / serratus anterior; rectus-abdominis and external-oblique (trunk hold)

exercises.direction: Push the floor away and finish with the shoulder blades spread around the ribcage.
exercises.camera: side view (the motion stays in the picture plane)
exercises.alternatives: Easier: Hands on a raised bench or table; knee push-up. Harder: Feet raised; slower lowering; added weight.

errors.description: Hips sag or pike and reps stop halfway.
errors.correction: Brace the trunk and squeeze the glutes so the body moves as one line, and lower until the chest is close to the floor.

errors.description: The hips sag toward the floor and the lower back arches.
errors.correction: Ribs down, glutes tight: shoulder, hip and ankle stay on one straight line.

errors.description: The elbows flare straight out to the sides.
errors.correction: Angle the elbows back, roughly 45 degrees from the body (a coaching convention).

errors.description: The reps stop halfway down.
errors.correction: Lower until the chest is close to the floor, then press back to straight arms.

cues: Hands just outside shoulder width, body one straight line from head to heels (ribs down, glutes tight).
Lower the chest to the floor with elbows angled back, not flared straight out.
Push the floor away and finish with the shoulder blades spread around the ribcage.

variations.name: Push-up plus
variations.note: Ludewig 2004: an extra shoulder-blade protraction at the top; highest serratus anterior activity of the push-up variants tested

execution: Place the hands on the floor just outside shoulder width, under the shoulders.
Step the feet back so the body is one straight line from head to heels; ribs down, glutes tight.
Lower the chest toward the floor with the elbows angled back, not flared straight out.
Push the floor away to straight arms, keeping the body line.
Finish with the shoulder blades spread around the ribcage.

exercises.name: Dumbbell bench press
exercises.start: Set the shoulder blades back and down against the bench, feet planted.

phases.description: Lower until the dumbbells are beside the chest with forearms vertical over the elbows.
Press up and slightly in, elbows about 45 degrees from the torso rather than flared wide.

muscles.fibres: pectoralis-major; triceps-brachii; deltoid (anterior fibres) / serratus anterior; biceps-brachii (long head, stabiliser)

exercises.direction: Press up and slightly in, elbows about 45 degrees from the torso rather than flared wide.
exercises.camera: side view (the motion stays in the picture plane)
exercises.alternatives: Easier: Floor press (shorter range); push-up variations. Harder: Incline bench; slower lowering; heavier dumbbells.

errors.description: Elbows flared straight out to the sides.
errors.correction: Aim for about 45 degrees between the upper arm and the torso.

errors.description: Bouncing the dumbbells off the chest.
errors.correction: Lower under control and pause briefly at the bottom.

cues: Set the shoulder blades back and down against the bench, feet planted.
Lower until the dumbbells are beside the chest with forearms vertical over the elbows.
Press up and slightly in, elbows about 45 degrees from the torso rather than flared wide.

variations.name: Neutral-grip press
variations.note: palms facing; often friendlier to the shoulder

variations.name: Incline press
variations.note: bench raised; more clavicular chest and front shoulder

variations.name: Floor press
variations.note: shorter range of motion

execution: Sit with the dumbbells on the thighs, lie back and kick them to the chest.
Set the shoulder blades back and down against the bench, feet planted.
Lower under control until the dumbbells are beside the chest, forearms vertical over the elbows.
Press up and slightly in until the arms are straight over the shoulders.
Pause at lockout, then repeat.
exercises.breathing: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you press (a common convention); avoid holding the breath for long.
visual_requirements: a FULL repetition: lockout, lowering, bottom, press, lockout
forearms vertical at every frame
dumbbell path as a slight arc
shoulder blades stay down on the bench
chest highlighted prime, triceps and front shoulder helpers

exercises.name: Dumbbell fly
exercises.start: Keep a soft, fixed bend in the elbows throughout.

phases.description: Open the arms in a wide arc until you feel a controlled stretch across the chest, no lower than you can control.
Bring the dumbbells back as if hugging a barrel.

muscles.fibres: pectoralis-major / deltoid (anterior fibres); biceps-brachii (stabiliser); serratus anterior

exercises.direction: Bring the dumbbells back as if hugging a barrel.
exercises.camera: above view (the motion stays in the picture plane)
exercises.alternatives: Easier: Resistance-band fly; lighter dumbbells. Harder: Incline bench; slow lowering; pause at the bottom.

errors.description: Straightening or bending the elbows through the rep so it turns into a press, or using a weight too heavy to control at the bottom.

cues: Keep a soft, fixed bend in the elbows throughout.
Open the arms in a wide arc until you feel a controlled stretch across the chest, no lower than you can control.
Bring the dumbbells back as if hugging a barrel.

exercises.name: Pull-up
exercises.start: Dead hang from the bar with an overhand (pronated) grip a little wider than the shoulders, arms straight, shoulder blades gently pulled down, not shrugged.

phases.description: Pull the elbows down toward the ribs until the chin clears the bar.
Lower under control to a full dead hang.

muscles.fibres: latissimus-dorsi; biceps-brachii; brachialis / trapezius (lower and middle fibres); rhomboids; deltoid (posterior fibres); pectoralis-major; brachioradialis / infraspinatus; forearm-flexors (grip); erector-spinae and external-oblique (trunk position)

exercises.direction: The body rises on a near-vertical line under the bar while the elbows travel down toward the ribs; the trunk stays still with no swing.
exercises.camera: back view for the shoulder blades and elbow path; side view for the trunk swing and the chin-over-bar line
exercises.alternatives: Easier: Band-assisted pull-up; slow lowering only (negatives); inverted row. Harder: Slower tempo; pause at the top; added weight.

errors.description: Swinging or kicking the body for momentum.
errors.correction: Hang still, brace the trunk, and pull from a dead hang each rep; use a band or negatives until you can.

errors.description: Starting from a bent-arm hang or stopping with the chin below the bar.
errors.correction: Start every rep from straight arms and pull until the chin clears the bar (Urbanczyk 2020: different phases emphasise different muscles, so the full range matters).

errors.description: The shoulders shrug up toward the ears in the hang or at the start of the pull.
errors.correction: Draw the shoulder blades gently down first, then pull the elbows toward the ribs.

cues: Start from a hang with the shoulder blades gently pulled down, not shrugged.
Pull the elbows down toward the ribs until the chin clears the bar.
Lower under control to a full hang.
exercises.source_claim: Latissimus dorsi and the elbow flexors as the movers with the scapular and trunk muscles assisting: Youdas 2010 (25 adults; a conventional pull-up recorded latissimus, biceps, infraspinatus, lower trapezius, pectoralis major, erector spinae and external oblique; latissimus activity was the highest of those muscles; the lower trapezius and pectoralis major led the pull and the biceps and latissimus completed it), Dickie 2017 (19 strength-trained men; similar shoulder-arm-forearm activity across grips; biceps, brachioradialis and pectoralis major were higher in the pulling phase than in the lowering phase), Urbanczyk 2020 (11 men; model-estimated muscle forces; the front pronated pull-up favoured biceps brachii and brachialis; full range matters), Prinold 2016 (11 participants; scapular kinematics differ between pull-up grips). Cues, including the kipping error, are coaching (NSCA Essentials 4e).

variations.name: Chin-up (supinated grip)
variations.note: Youdas 2010 (25 adults): higher biceps and pectoralis major activity than the pull-up; lower trapezius higher in the pull-up

variations.name: Neutral-grip pull-up
variations.note: Dickie 2017 (19 men): lower middle trapezius activity than the pronated grip; overall similar activity across grips

variations.name: Wide-grip pull-up
variations.note: Urbanczyk 2020 (11 men): relatively more latissimus activity (model-estimated); Prinold 2016: wide and reverse grips showed kinematics linked with higher impingement risk

execution: Take an overhand grip a little wider than the shoulders and hang with straight arms.
Draw the shoulder blades gently down, without shrugging.
Pull the elbows toward the ribs until the chin clears the bar.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower under control to a full dead hang.

tempo.note: illustrative; 'bottom' here is the dead hang

exercises.breathing: Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower (a common convention).
visual_requirements: bar fixed; the body rises under it
pronated grip: palms face away, hands a little wider than the shoulders
starts from a full dead hang with straight arms
chin clears the bar at the top
trunk still, no swing or kick
latissimus dorsi, biceps and brachialis highlighted as movers; scapular and trunk muscles as helpers
exercises.experience: some pulling strength, or use band assistance

role_basis.latissimus-dorsi: Measured in Youdas 2010 (highest of the muscles recorded); modelled in Urbanczyk 2020; extends and adducts the arm (OpenStax 11.5).
role_basis.biceps-brachii: Measured in Youdas 2010 and Dickie 2017; modelled in Urbanczyk 2020; elbow flexor (OpenStax 11.5).
role_basis.brachialis: Model-estimated (not measured EMG) in Urbanczyk 2020; elbow flexor (OpenStax 11.5). Deep.
role_basis.trapezius: Lower trapezius measured in Youdas 2010; middle trapezius measured in Dickie 2017.
role_basis.rhomboids: Retract the scapula (OpenStax 11.5). Anatomy, not measured in the pull-up sources.
role_basis.deltoid: Posterior fibres extend the arm (OpenStax 11.5). Anatomy, not measured in the pull-up sources.
role_basis.infraspinatus: Measured in Youdas 2010; rotator-cuff stabiliser of the shoulder.
role_basis.erector-spinae: Measured in Youdas 2010 (lower activity than the movers); holds the hanging trunk.
role_basis.external-oblique: Measured in Youdas 2010 (lower activity than the movers); anatomy and the study support a trunk-holding role, not more.

exercises.name: One-arm dumbbell row
exercises.start: One hand and the same-side knee on the flat bench, the other foot on the floor, back flat and hips level, the dumbbell hanging at arm's length.

phases.description: Pull the elbow toward the hip rather than straight up, shoulder blade moving with the arm.
Lower to a full stretch without twisting the torso.

muscles.fibres: latissimus-dorsi; rhomboids; trapezius (middle and lower fibres) / deltoid (posterior fibres); biceps-brachii; brachialis / erector-spinae (trunk position); forearm-flexors (grip)

exercises.direction: The dumbbell travels in a near-vertical arc from beside the knee to the hip; the elbow passes close to the ribs and the trunk stays still.
exercises.camera: side view for the elbow path and back angle; above or front view to catch torso twist
exercises.alternatives: Easier: Chest-supported row on an incline bench; resistance-band row; lighter dumbbell. Harder: Pause at the top; slower lowering; heavier dumbbell.

errors.description: Twisting and heaving the torso to swing the weight, with a shortened range.
errors.correction: Keep the shoulders and hips square to the floor; lighten the dumbbell until only the arm and shoulder blade move.

errors.description: The elbow flares out and the dumbbell is pulled straight up toward the chest.
errors.correction: Pull the elbow toward the hip, close to the ribs.

errors.description: The back rounds or the trunk drops at the bottom of the rep.
errors.correction: Keep the back flat and the head in line with the spine; stop the stretch where the back stays flat.

errors.description: Stopping the lowering well short of a full stretch.
errors.correction: Let the arm straighten and the shoulder blade reach forward each rep, with the trunk still.

cues: Support one hand and knee on the bench, back flat and hips level.
Pull the elbow toward the hip rather than straight up, shoulder blade moving with the arm.
Lower to a full stretch without twisting the torso.
exercises.source_claim: Back and scapular muscles as movers with the elbow flexors helping: Andersen 2012 (17 women; a one-arm row activated the middle trapezius over the upper trapezius and, at both effort levels, the lower trapezius over the upper trapezius; the abstract does not describe the row set-up), Fenwick 2009 (7 men; the standing one-armed cable row challenged the torsional capability of the trunk muscles; the inverted row gave the highest latissimus activity and the bent-over row the largest lumbar load; no dumbbell bench row was studied). Latissimus dorsi, rhomboid, posterior deltoid and brachialis roles are anatomy (OpenStax A&P 2e 11.5), not measured in this set-up. Cues are coaching (NSCA Essentials 4e).

variations.name: Chest-supported one-arm row
variations.note: pad or incline bench removes the trunk demand

variations.name: Standing one-arm cable row
variations.note: Fenwick 2009 (7 men): challenged the torsional capability of the trunk muscles

variations.name: Bent-over two-arm row
variations.note: Fenwick 2009 (7 men): large symmetric back activity but the largest lumbar spine load of the rows studied

execution: Place one hand and the same-side knee on a flat bench, the other foot on the floor.
Set a flat back with the hips level and take the dumbbell at arm's length.
Pull the elbow toward the hip, the shoulder blade moving back with the arm.
Pause briefly with the dumbbell by the ribs.
Lower to a full stretch without twisting the torso.

tempo.note: illustrative; 'bottom' here is the arm hanging straight

exercises.breathing: Exhale as you row, inhale as you lower (a common convention).

back flat and hips level at every frame
elbow travels toward the hip, close to the ribs
shoulders stay square to the floor; no torso twist
latissimus dorsi, rhomboids and trapezius highlighted as movers; elbow flexors as helpers

exercises.name: Conventional barbell deadlift
exercises.start: Feet about hip-width, the bar over the midfoot, hands just outside the knees, hips above the knees, shoulders slightly in front of the bar, back flat and braced.

phases.description: Push the floor away: the bar rises close to the shins and thighs while the hips and shoulders rise together, then the hips come through to standing tall.
Hinge the hips back with the back flat, the bar sliding down the thighs, then bend the knees once it passes them and set the plates on the floor.

joints: ankle plantar flexion from a dorsiflexed start
exercises.direction: The bar travels in a near-vertical line over the midfoot and stays close to the legs; off the floor the hips and shoulders rise at the same rate.
exercises.camera: side view for the bar path and back angle; front for stance and grip width
exercises.alternatives: Easier: Romanian deadlift; trap-bar deadlift; pulling from blocks (a raised start). Harder: Pause just below the knee; deficit deadlift (standing on a low platform); heavier load.

errors.description: The lower back rounds as the bar leaves the floor.
errors.correction: Brace and set the back flat before the pull, take the slack out of the bar first, and lighten the load until the position holds.

errors.description: The bar drifts forward, away from the legs.
errors.correction: Start with the bar over the midfoot and keep it brushing the legs all the way up.

errors.description: The hips rise first and the chest stays down, so the pull turns into a stiff-legged lift.
errors.correction: Push the floor away so the hips and shoulders rise together until the bar passes the knees.

errors.description: Leaning back and over-arching the lower back at lockout.
errors.correction: Finish standing tall: hips through, glutes tight, ribs down.

cues: Bar over the midfoot, hands just outside the knees, back flat and braced.
Push the floor away; hips and shoulders rise together.
Keep the bar brushing the legs all the way up.
Stand tall at the top; do not lean back.
exercises.source_claim: Muscle roles from EMG: Escamilla 2002 (13 athletes), Lee 2018 (21 men), Martín-Fuentes 2020 (systematic review), Neto 2020 (systematic review, gluteus maximus); joint moments from Escamilla 2000 (24 competition lifters); adductor magnus as a hip extensor from OpenStax A&P 2e 11.6. execution: Stand with the midfoot under the bar, feet about hip-width.
Hinge and bend the knees to grip the bar just outside the knees.
Set the back flat, brace, and take the slack out of the bar.

Once the bar passes the knees, drive the hips through and stand tall.
Hinge back down the same path and set the plates on the floor.

tempo.note: illustrative; each rep starts from the floor (dead stop)

exercises.breathing: Breathe in and brace before the bar leaves the floor, exhale near or after lockout (a common convention); avoid holding the breath for long.
camera_angles: side (about az 72 so the plates do not hide the head)
visual_requirements: bar stays over the midfoot and close to the legs at every frame
back stays flat from the floor to lockout (the back angle changes, the spine shape does not)
hips and shoulders rise together until the bar passes the knees
full lockout standing tall with no lean back
plates return to the floor each rep
gluteus maximus, hamstrings and quadriceps highlighted as prime movers; erector spinae as a helper

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift (barbell)
exercises.start: Stand tall holding the bar at the hips with straight arms, feet about hip-width, knees slightly bent, back flat.

phases.description: Push the hips back; the bar slides down the thighs to about the knees or just below, as far as the back stays flat, knees staying softly bent.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall, the bar staying close to the legs.

exercises.direction: The hips travel back and forward; the bar moves almost straight down and up over the midfoot, close to the legs, while the knee angle barely changes.
exercises.camera: side view for the hip hinge, the knee angle and the bar path
exercises.alternatives: Easier: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift; hip hinge with a dowel along the back; shorter range. Harder: Single-leg Romanian deadlift; slower lowering; pause at the bottom.

errors.description: The back rounds to reach the bar lower.
errors.correction: Stop the descent where the back stops being flat; the range comes from the hips, not the spine.

errors.description: The knees bend more and more until the lift becomes a squat or a conventional deadlift.
errors.correction: Keep the knees softly bent and almost still; push the hips back instead of down.

errors.description: The bar swings forward away from the thighs.
errors.correction: Keep the bar sliding down the thighs, over the midfoot.

cues: Soft knees, then push the hips back.
Bar slides down the thighs; stop when the back would round.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall.

exercises.name: Forward lunge (dumbbells)
exercises.start: Stand tall, feet hip-width, a dumbbell in each hand at the sides.

phases.description: Step forward and lower straight down until the back knee is just above the floor, front foot flat.
Push through the whole front foot to step back to standing.

joints: front hip and knee flexion then extension
exercises.direction: The body drops straight down between the feet; the front knee travels over the front foot and in line with the toes.
exercises.camera: side view for the step length and both knee angles; front for front-knee tracking
exercises.alternatives: Easier: Bodyweight lunge; reverse lunge (step back); split squat (feet stay put); hold a support. Harder: Walking lunge; heavier dumbbells; front foot on a low step.

errors.description: The front knee collapses inward.
errors.correction: Keep the front knee in line with the second and third toes.

errors.description: The step is too short, the front heel lifts and the weight rolls onto the toes.
errors.correction: Step long enough that the whole front foot stays planted.

errors.description: The feet land on one line, so the body wobbles.
errors.correction: Keep the feet about hip-width apart side to side, like train tracks.

errors.description: The trunk pitches forward uncontrolled at the bottom.
errors.correction: Stay tall. A deliberate, controlled forward lean is a variation that shifts work toward the hip extensors (Farrokhi 2008), not a collapse.

cues: Step forward and drop straight down between the feet.
Front knee in line with the toes, whole front foot planted.
Push through the front foot to step back.

exercises.name: Forearm plank
exercises.start: Forearms on the mat with the elbows under the shoulders, legs straight, toes on the floor, knees down.

phases.description: Lift the knees and hips until the body is one straight line from head to heels.
Hold the line: ribs down, glutes tight, breathing steadily.

exercises.camera: side view (the body line is the whole lesson)
exercises.alternatives: Easier: Plank from the knees; hands on a bench (incline plank); shorter holds. Harder: Long-lever plank (elbows further forward); plank with a posterior pelvic tilt; plank on a suspension trainer or ball; longer holds.

errors.description: The hips sag toward the floor and the lower back arches.
errors.correction: Squeeze the glutes, draw the ribs down, and push the floor away through the forearms.

errors.description: The hips pike up above the line.
errors.correction: Lower the hips until shoulder, hip and ankle line up.

errors.description: Holding the breath through the hold.
errors.correction: Keep breathing steadily; shorten the hold if needed.

cues: Elbows under the shoulders.
One straight line from head to heels: ribs down, glutes tight.
Breathe steadily; stop when the line breaks.

exercises.name: Leg press (45-degree sled)
exercises.start: Back and hips flat against the pad, feet about shoulder-width in the middle of the platform, knees in line with the toes; release the safety stops.

phases.description: Let the platform come down by bending the knees toward the chest, as far as the hips stay on the pad.
Press the platform away through the whole foot to straight legs, without snapping the knees into a hard lock.

joints: pelvis and back stay on the pad
exercises.direction: The platform slides along its rail; the feet stay fixed on it and the hips stay on the seat, so the knees travel toward the chest and back.
exercises.camera: side view for depth and the pelvis on the pad; front for knee tracking
exercises.alternatives: Easier: Lighter load; shorter range; single sets with long rest. Harder: Single-leg leg press; slower lowering; pause at the bottom.

errors.description: Going so deep that the hips roll off the pad and the lower back rounds.
errors.correction: Stop the descent while the hips stay flat on the pad.

errors.description: Snapping the knees into a hard lock at the top.
errors.correction: Press to straight legs under control (a coaching convention).

errors.description: The knees collapse inward as the platform comes down.
errors.correction: Keep the knees in line with the toes.

errors.description: The heels lift off the platform at the bottom.
errors.correction: Keep the whole foot on the platform; move the feet a little higher if needed.

cues: Hips and back stay on the pad.
Knees in line with the toes, whole foot on the platform.
Press away smoothly to straight legs; no hard snap at the top.

exercises.start: Seated with the thighs under the pad, an overhand grip a little wider than the shoulders, arms straight overhead, chest up.

errors.correction: Start the pull by drawing the shoulder blades down, then bend the elbows.

errors.description: Stopping halfway up on the return.
errors.correction: Let the arms straighten fully overhead each rep.

exercises.name: Seated cable row
exercises.start: Sit tall with the feet on the plate, knees slightly bent, a neutral-grip handle at arm's length, trunk upright.

phases.description: Row the handle to the lower ribs, elbows close and back, shoulder blades drawing together.
Let the arms straighten and the shoulder blades move forward under control, the trunk staying upright.

exercises.direction: The handle travels in a straight horizontal line toward the lower ribs; the trunk stays upright and still.
exercises.camera: side view for the handle path, elbow path and trunk angle; back for the shoulder blades
exercises.alternatives: Easier: Lighter stack; chest-supported row; resistance-band row. Harder: Single-arm cable row; slower lowering; pause with the shoulder blades together.

errors.description: Rocking the trunk back and forth to move the weight.
errors.correction: Keep the trunk upright and still; only the arms and shoulder blades move.

errors.description: The shoulders shrug toward the ears at the end of the pull.
errors.correction: Draw the shoulder blades back and down, not up.

errors.description: The back rounds forward at the stretch.
errors.correction: Let the shoulder blades reach forward, but keep the trunk tall.

cues: Sit tall, knees soft, trunk still.
Row the handle to the lower ribs, elbows close.
Shoulder blades together at the end, then reach forward under control.
exercises.source_claim: Latissimus dorsi and the middle trapezius/rhomboid group as prime movers with elbow flexors as helpers: Lehman 2004 (the seated row produced the highest middle trapezius/rhomboid activity of the four tasks and a high latissimus-to-biceps ratio; actively retracting the scapula did not change middle trapezius/rhomboid activity). Posterior deltoid and teres major anatomy: OpenStax A&P 2e 11.5. Cues are coaching (NSCA Essentials 4e).

variations.note: elbows out; more upper back

variations.name: Single-arm cable row
variations.note: one side at a time; the trunk resists rotation

variations.name: Chest-supported row
variations.note: pad on the chest removes the trunk demand

execution: Sit with the feet on the plate and knees slightly bent.
Take the handle and sit tall with straight arms.
Row the handle to the lower ribs, elbows close to the body.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together briefly.
Return slowly to straight arms without rocking the trunk.

tempo.note: illustrative; 'bottom' here is the handle at the ribs

exercises.breathing: Exhale as you row, inhale as you return (a common convention).
visual_requirements: cable stays taut; the weight stack rises as the handle comes in
handle path horizontal to the lower ribs
trunk upright and still at every frame
shoulder blades visibly retract at the end of the pull (back view)
latissimus dorsi, rhomboids and trapezius highlighted as prime movers

role_basis.latissimus-dorsi: Measured in Lehman 2004 (high latissimus-to-biceps ratio in the seated row); extends the arm (OpenStax 11.5).
role_basis.rhomboids: Lehman 2004: middle trapezius/rhomboid activity was highest in the seated row; retract the scapula (OpenStax 11.5).
role_basis.trapezius: Lehman 2004 (middle trapezius/rhomboid group); retracts the scapula (OpenStax 11.5).
role_basis.deltoid: Posterior fibres extend the arm (OpenStax 11.5). Anatomy, not measured in the row source.
role_basis.teres-major: Extends the arm (OpenStax 11.5). Anatomy, not measured in the row source.
role_basis.erector-spinae: Holds the trunk upright against the pull. Anatomy and coaching, not measured in the row source.

exercises.name: Barbell bench press
exercises.start: Lie with the eyes under the bar, feet planted, shoulder blades pulled back and down, an overhand grip a little wider than the shoulders, wrists stacked over the forearms.

phases.description: Lower the bar to the lower chest with the forearms about vertical under it.
Press the bar up and slightly back to straight arms over the shoulders.

exercises.direction: The bar moves in a shallow curve between the lower chest and a point over the shoulders; the forearms stay about vertical under it.
exercises.camera: side view for the bar path and forearm angle; three-quarter from the foot end for elbow angle
exercises.alternatives: Easier: Push-up; dumbbell bench press; floor press (shorter range). Harder: Pause at the chest; close-grip bench press; heavier load.

errors.description: Elbows flared straight out to the sides.
errors.correction: Tuck the elbows to a moderate angle from the torso so the forearms stay vertical under the bar.

errors.description: Bouncing the bar off the chest.
errors.correction: Lower under control and touch the chest lightly, or pause.

errors.description: The hips lift off the bench to press.
errors.correction: Keep the hips and shoulders on the bench and drive through the feet.

errors.description: The wrists bend back under the bar.
errors.correction: Stack the bar over the wrists and forearms.

cues: Shoulder blades back and down, feet planted.
Lower the bar to the lower chest, forearms vertical.
Press up and slightly back to straight arms over the shoulders.
exercises.source_claim: Pectoralis major and triceps brachii as prime movers with the anterior deltoid as a helper: Stastny 2017 (systematic review of 14 studies: pectoralis major and triceps activity similar and greater than anterior deltoid). Biceps as a stabiliser: Saeterbakken 2011 (12 men; biceps activity rose with stability demands). Grip-width notes: Lehman 2005 (12 men). Cues are coaching (NSCA Essentials 4e).

variations.note: Lehman 2005 (12 men): narrower grips increased triceps activity and decreased sternocostal pectoralis activity

variations.note: bench raised

variations.note: Saeterbakken 2011 (12 men): pectoralis major and anterior deltoid activity similar to the barbell; less biceps activity

execution: Lie on the bench with the eyes under the bar and the feet planted.
Grip a little wider than the shoulders and set the shoulder blades back and down.
Unrack the bar to straight arms over the shoulders.
Lower under control to the lower chest, forearms vertical.
Press up and slightly back to straight arms; rack the bar at the end of the set.
exercises.breathing: Breathe in and brace as the bar comes down, exhale as you press (a common convention); avoid long breath holds.
camera_angles: side (about az 72 so the plates do not hide the head)
visual_requirements: a FULL repetition: unrack, lower, touch, press, lockout
forearms about vertical under the bar at every frame
bar touches the lower chest and finishes over the shoulders
hips and shoulder blades stay on the bench
pectoralis major and triceps highlighted as prime; front deltoid as helper
exercises.experience: some coaching advised; use a spotter or safety arms

role_basis.pectoralis-major: Stastny 2017 (systematic review): among the most active muscles in the flat bench press; Lehman 2005 and Saeterbakken 2011 measured it.
role_basis.triceps-brachii: Stastny 2017: activity similar to pectoralis major; Lehman 2005 (more with narrower grips).
role_basis.deltoid: Stastny 2017: anterior deltoid activity lower than pectoralis major and triceps, so a helper here.
role_basis.biceps-brachii: Saeterbakken 2011: activity rises with stability demands (Smith machine < barbell < dumbbells); a stabiliser.
role_basis.rotator-cuff: Surrounds and steadies the shoulder joint (OpenStax 11.5). Deep; anatomy, not measured.
